hook.text: In Tibet, bodies are cut into pieces and fed to vultures on a mountaintop. It's considered the most generous act.

buildup.text: Sky burial, called 'jhator,' treats the body as an empty vessel. The soul has already departed.

discovery.text: Tibet's frozen ground makes digging graves impossible. Scarce wood makes cremation impractical. Vultures solve both.

twist.text: China banned sky burials during the Cultural Revolution. Tibetans practiced them secretly and resumed when bans lifted.

climax.text: Vulture populations are declining due to veterinary drugs. Sky burials now face an ecological crisis.

punchline.text: The most humble burial needs the wildest partners.

quiz.question: Why is sky burial practical in Tibet?
options: The ground is frozen and wood is scarce
